patches.old: The exact count is the number of distinct compiled circuits, including any wrappers, in a frozen circuit inventory. The 235 pre-dedup review identifiers, 20 families and seven layers describe review scope. None of them is a setup count. The circuit manifest is not frozen, so no total can be assigned yet.
patches.new: In the common two-phase architecture, the exact count is one phase 2 per distinct compiled circuit, including any wrappers, in a frozen circuit inventory, plus one phase 1 per compatible parameter set the inventory uses. Circuits on one curve and format share a phase 1 whose capacity covers the largest of them. An existing compatible phase 1 can be reused. The 235 pre-dedup review identifiers, 20 families and seven layers describe review scope, not a setup count. The inventory is not frozen, so no total can be assigned yet.

patches.old: This holds only if every circuit uses the same curve, fits the phase-1 capacity and accepts its format, and only if each phase has a verified transcript with at least one honest participant.
patches.new: The count holds only if every circuit uses the same curve and format and fits the shared phase-1 capacity. Smaller circuits need no extra phase 1. Each stage yields sound keys only if its transcript verifies and at least one participant in it was honest.
